page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-384-metal is a bare-metal server engineered for enterprise environments that demand massive memory density and dedicated compute resources. Operating on the x86_64 processor architecture, the system provides 384 dedicated vCPUs paired with 3,072 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, placing it among high-capacity platforms capable of sustaining memory-intensive tasks without host-level contention.

The machine operates as a pure bare-metal platform without a hypervisor layer, affording direct execution on the underlying physical hardware. It includes no integrated GPU accelerators or onboard local disk storage, meaning all persistent and scratch storage operations rely entirely on external network-attached volumes. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled with the instance, requiring network provisioning through VPC resources.

From a qualitative efficiency perspective, c4d-highmem-384-metal represents an infrastructure tier designed for extreme resource consolidation rather than distributed, lightweight tasks. The dense core count combined with three terabytes of RAM minimizes multi-instance management overhead by housing large datasets within a single physical footprint. Because it omits specialized accelerators and physical storage, spending remains strictly isolated to dedicated CPU threads and vast system memory.

This hardware profile matches enterprise workloads requiring large in-memory caches, memory-bound transactional databases, large-scale analytics platforms, and extract-transform-load (ETL) processing. It is also suitable for extensive data modeling and batch compute jobs that benefit from direct hardware access across hundreds of dedicated processor threads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-384-metal is a high-density bare-metal server configured for enterprise-scale in-memory workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 3,072 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The bare-metal design eliminates virtualization overhead, giving applications direct hardware control and predictable execution across all processing threads. The server does not bundle dedicated graphics hardware or integrated local storage, requiring external persistent network storage solutions for disk operations and state retention. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addressing is omitted. Given its substantial physical resource pool, this bare-metal offering maximizes core density and memory consolidation, trading local storage conveniences for raw hardware throughput. It is ideally matched for large-scale relational and in-memory databases, memory-bound enterprise software, massive analytics tasks, and heavy computational batch processing that demand uninterrupted access to extensive compute and RAM resources.
